summary: The starter prompt clearly states the goal (Python LangChain agent combining DB aggregation and live web signals) and the agent framework. The run environment (live DocumentDB cluster, DATABASE name, and env var for the URI) is provided in the supplied skill_md, so the build can start. Several important implementation details are left unspecified (Python version, exact pymongo version, collection schema and seed data, indexes, AI model choices, web-search API, run/test/README specifics), and the builder will make reasonable defaults for these unless the author clarifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "run a DocumentDB aggregation pipeline comparing sales velocity across seasons" and "produce a ranked list of rising and declining categories"
rubric.note: Business problem, user outcome and what sample demonstrates are clearly stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain agent with two tools"
rubric.note: Single LangChain agent with two tools is explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python LangChain agent"; skill_md: "python and pip resolve to a virtual environment"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will target a modern Python 3.x runtime (assume Python 3.10 or 3.11) and create a venv; requirements.txt will target that.
rubric.note: Language is specified but no concrete Python version is given.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requires a DocumentDB aggregation tool that connects using a MongoDB driver; reference_requirements requires pymongo in requirements.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use pymongo (the official Python MongoDB driver); pin a reasonably recent, MongoDB-7.0-compatible version (e.g., pymongo >=4.3, often pinned to 4.4.x or latest stable 4.x). Follow the documentdb-driver guidance to use a singleton MongoClient.
rubric.note: The driver type (pymongo) is implied by reference requirements, and the documentdb-driver skill covers instantiation patterns, but no concrete version or version-range is specified in the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable..." and "use the database named sample_retail_17"
rubric.note: Run environment provided in skill_md fixes the target cluster and database to use.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI" and "Never write its value into any file, log... use .env.example with a placeholder"
rubric.note: Env-var-based secret handling is explicitly given.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "group sales by product category and by season... return structured JSON/dict records containing category, season, sales_count, sales_velocity, and percent_change" (in reference requirements)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create/use a 'sales' collection in database sample_retail_17 with documents like: { _id, product_id, category: str, sale_date: ISODate, quantity: int, price: number } and derive sales_count/velocity from sale_date and quantity/price. Season will be derived from sale_date (e.g., Q1, Q2, or meteorological seasons).
rubric.note: High-level fields needed for the aggregation are described, but exact collection name, field names and types are not. The documentdb-data-modeling skill can guide decisions, but the developer will pick a conventional 'sales' schema.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include a small idempotent seed script (e.g., scripts/seed_data.py) that creates a 'sales' collection and inserts synthetic sample data across several categories and seasons; the script should be runnable multiple times without duplicating data (use upsert or dedupe on a unique transaction id).
rubric.note: No source, size, licensing or seed-loading instructions are provided in the starter prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requires an aggregation pipeline computing sales_velocity and percent_change (in reference requirements) but does not specify indexes.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create at least indexes to support the aggregation: an index on { category: 1, sale_date: 1 } (or separate indexes on category and sale_date) and any needed multikey or TTL indexes if time-based retention is implemented. If vectors are used for any similarity, the vector index will be created with parameters suitable for the sample size.
rubric.note: Index guidance is available via documentdb-indexing, but exact index shapes and parameters are not specified in the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt mentions LangChain and a web search tool but does not specify embedding/chat models or providers.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use environment variables for any model credentials (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) and choose a commonly used embedding model (e.g., OpenAI 'text-embedding-3-small' or equivalent) and a chat LLM for agent reasoning (e.g., OpenAI gpt-4o or user-configurable). Embedding dimensionality and vector-index settings will be set to match the chosen embedding model (builder will document the mapping).
rubric.note: No explicit model names, dimensions, or providers are specified; the documentdb-vector-search skill can guide index choices once a model is selected.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain agent... produce a ranked list" and reference_requirements: "end-to-end example run (script or notebook)"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a CLI entrypoint (e.g., python main.py) and an example notebook/cell; main.py loads env vars, runs the aggregation tool, runs the web search tool, invokes the LangChain agent, and prints the ranked rising/declining lists to stdout in JSON.
rubric.note: The prompt requires an agent as the main executable, but does not spell out whether to expose an HTTP API or CLI; builder will choose CLI + notebook examples.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use."
rubric.note: The environment prohibits provisioning new clusters for this sample; use the existing cluster.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include a README and example commands: pip install -r requirements.txt; cp .env.example .env and edit; python main.py --example-run; a notebook cell demonstrating the example run. Tests may be included but will be annotated to skip live-cluster integration unless env var TEST_WITH_LIVE=true is set.
rubric.note: No explicit run/test commands or success criteria are provided in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat the reference_requirements as the acceptance checklist: agent runs, tools registered, aggregation returns structured records, web search returns signals with URLs/timestamps, combined scores computed programmatically, and an end-to-end example run included.
rubric.note: Prompt lacks explicit acceptance criteria; the reference requirements provide what is needed but are not embedded in the starter prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid provisioning cloud resources, keep dataset small to control cost, not include secrets in code, and document limits/cost implications in the README.
rubric.note: No explicit cost or compliance constraints are stated in the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder..."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will follow typical sample conventions: top-level README.md documenting prerequisites/setup/run/cleanup, src/ or app/ for code, scripts/ for seed and admin scripts, requirements.txt pinned, .env.example present, and tests/ containing unit tests that run without a live cluster.
rubric.note: Some hints exist in skill_md (.env.example) but full repo layout conventions are not provided.

contradictions: The starter prompt says "Using the DocumentDB skill" but there is no single installed skill named exactly "DocumentDB" — there are multiple documentdb-* skills (documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection, etc.). The prompt's reference to a single "DocumentDB skill" is ambiguous.
questions_for_author: Which web search API should be used at runtime (Bing Web Search, Google Custom Search, SerpAPI, other)? Provide preferred API and env-var name for its key.

Which embedding and chat model/provider should the sample use (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, local LLM)? Please specify model names or allow the builder to use configurable environment variables (e.g., EMBEDDING_MODEL, LLM_MODEL).

Should the sample include an idempotent seed script with synthetic data, or is there existing sample data in the provided cluster to use? If seed script is required, confirm the intended collection name (default: 'sales').
Do you prefer a CLI entrypoint (python main.py), an HTTP API, or a notebook-driven demo as the primary sample surface?
Do you require pinned dependency versions in requirements.txt and unit tests that run without a live cluster?
requirements_at_risk: Provide a requirements file listing packages used (must include pymongo and langchain) — prompt mentions Python/LangChain but does not explicitly require or specify requirements.txt format or pinned versions; builder will add it but it's not in the prompt.
Seed script that loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — starter prompt does not mention a seed script or idempotency.
The vector index dimensions must match the embedding model's output — no embedding model is specified in the prompt, so the correct dimensionality is at risk.
Vector index parameters chosen for the sample size, and README guidance for changing them — prompt doesn't specify index parameters or sample size guidance.

One database client is created and reused across requests (singleton MongoClient) — the documentdb-driver skill suggests this, but the prompt does not explicitly require it; it's at risk if the builder forgets it.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — web-search behavior and error handling are not specified in the prompt.
Search results include the similarity score — prompt requires web signals with relevance/confidence but doesn't explicitly require similarity scores in any vector search; risk is moderate.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt — prompt doesn't require pinned versions; builders may or may not pin them.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — prompt requires live web searches and DB access for the example run, but doesn't mandate local-unit tests; this is at risk.

Infrastructure for the cluster provided as code (Azure DocumentDB resource type) — prompt and skill_md say a cluster already exists and prohibit provisioning; infra-as-code is not part of the requested sample and is at risk of being omitted.

README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — prompt doesn't require a README explicitly though a sample should include it; this is at risk if the builder omits thorough documentation.
The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout and no former/neighbouring product name — the prompt doesn't specify naming conventions; builders may vary naming unless instructed.
